Subject: Demo interruption — sessions routed to slow variant, can we rollback?

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Quick heads-up from this afternoon's customer demo: several of our sessions started getting 700-1200ms p95 latencies and occasionally 5xxs when the model variant changed mid-session. The UX team saw truncation and the demo had to be cut short.

We're running the POC account under deal DEAL-2347; this was during the guided demo flow (multiple short messages, lots of small prompts). Can you confirm whether you can: 1) rapidly pin us back to the previous model variant or 2) disable the variant rollout just for OrbitHealth?

We need an answer within the next 24 hours because the procurement team is asking about stability before finalizing signatures. I've attached the session logs we captured and a short video from the demo.

Attachments: session_logs_20270428.zip (log archive)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Demo interruption — sessions routed to slow variant, can we rollback?

Short summary from runtime side after an initial log sweep: we did have a progressive rollout of Variant-B for the small-context generator class between 15:40–16:25 PDT. For most customers it looked fine, but we've got a bug where session_override TTLs were not being honored on a subset of routing keys due to a race in the heartbeat / expiry path. That matches the symptom where ongoing sessions suddenly see a different routing decision mid-session.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked by speed):
1) Admin API rollback: pin OrbitHealth's routing key to Variant-A (previous stable) using: curl -X POST https://admin.redwoodinference.com/api/v1/routing/pin -d '{"account_id":"DEAL-2347","variant":"Variant-A"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
   - Effect: near-instant; non-disruptive to other accounts.
2) Short maintenance patch: apply hotfix to heartbeat expiry path (requires 20–30 minute maintenance with short reconnects).
3) Workaround: increase client side retry/backoff to avoid hitting the transient path (not ideal for demos).

I've opened JIRA SUP-7890 and attached a sample of the affected session ids. If SalesOps wants the immediate rollback we need: confirmation to proceed and the list of OrbitHealth routing keys to pin (I can do a targeted pin without a full org-wide rollback).

[Attachment: excerpt_session_ids.txt]

—
Dev Patel
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 19:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo interruption — Demo routing rollback plan (targeted)

Thanks — good catch, Dev.

A couple operational notes / safer plan so we don't risk collateral impact:
- We can avoid a global rollback by using the routing-key pin approach. That allows us to scope to only OrbitHealth and keeps the progressive rollout running for others.
- I'll coordinate with Ops to run the pin in a canary fashion: 1) pin the single primary routing key for OrbitHealth; 2) observe for 10 minutes at p95/5xx; 3) if stable, pin any remaining keys.
- Timeline: I can execute tonight at 20:00 PDT if OrbitHealth agrees. Execution is ~3–5 minutes but we want the 10-minute observation window.

Logistics needed from SalesEng / Customer: list of routing keys / session ids OR confirmation that the account routing key is DEAL-2347-primary (if that's the case I can proceed).

I'll also attach the internal runbook for targeted pins to the Jira ticket SUP-7890.

—

Subject: Re: Demo interruption — proposed targeted rollback for OrbitHealth

Hi Emily — thanks again for the capture. We've triaged this and have a low-risk plan:

Proposed (targeted) plan — requires your approval to proceed:
1) We will pin OrbitHealth's primary routing key to Variant-A (previous stable) at 20:00 PDT tonight. Execution window is ~3–5 minutes and we'll monitor p95 and error rates for 10 minutes after.
2) If everything looks good, we'll pin any secondary routing keys for the account to Variant-A.
3) Dev will push a fix for the heartbeat expiry race in the next release; Jira SUP-7890 is tracking the fix and timeline.

What we need from you now:
- Confirm you approve the targeted pin at 20:00 PDT tonight OR request an immediate rollback now (we can do immediate but prefer the observation window).
- If you have any preferred maintenance constraints, let us know.

I've attached the session logs and a short note on expected SLOs for your reference. Once you approve, Jonas and Dev will run the pin and I'll provide a short summary back to procurement for signatures.
